subject: Request: Latency SLO carveout & service credit cap for Skyline Health
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@skylinehealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@skylinehealth.com>, Chris Park <chris.park@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 17 Jun 2028 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Request: latency SLO carveout & service credit language (Skyline pilot)

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo today — the team was impressed with the latency and prediction consistency. Before we go to legal, our security and platform teams flagged two items where Skyline needs an explicit concession for this pilot:

- A temporary latency SLO acceptance: for the first 90 days, we need an expanded latency SLO of 99.5% for 95th percentile latency (current commercial SLO requests 99.9%).
- A cap on service credits: due to procurement policy, Skyline requires a fixed service credit cap of 12.5% of monthly invoice for any SLO failures during the pilot.

We understand these are non-standard. We are running a regulated pilot and cannot commit without those terms being visible to finance/legal. Could you confirm if Redwood can approve a 90-day carveout and the 12.5% cap, and whether that would require executive sign-off?

Attaching a short summary from our side. If it's helpful, we can take a quick call tomorrow.

Best,
Elena Morales
Senior Program Manager — Cloud Partnerships
Skyline Health
(attachment: skyline_pilot_requirements.pdf)
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 Jun 2028 19:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latency SLO carveout & service credit language (Skyline pilot)

Elena — really appreciate the clarity and the prompt follow-up.

Short answer: we can usually handle limited pilot SLO adjustments, but a service-credit cap at 12.5% and a 90-day carveout are outside our standard playbook and will need deal-desk + Exec sign-off.

Next steps from our side:
- Marissa, can you run the risk/precedent check and draft a redline for the SLO appendix?
- Ben, please pull recent similar precedents (pilot SLOs & caps) and any commercial offsets (discounts/credits) we offered.
- Elena, we'll come back with an internal recommendation by Monday EOD. If approved, Jonas will need to sign off on the non-standard remedy and any discount tied to it.

Happy to jump on a 20-min call with your contracts team if that speeds things up.

Thanks — Avery
Avery Johnson
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latency SLO carveout & service credit language (Skyline pilot)

Folks — reviewed Skyline's ask. Summary of our assessment:

- Risk/precedent: We have approved 90-day pilot carveouts before but typically limited the service credit cap to 10% of monthly invoice. 12.5% is above precedent and increases commercial exposure.
- Mitigations: We can combine a capped credit with a temporary discount (to offset risk) and require a technical validation period (instrumentation + synthetic tests) to trigger the carveout.

Proposal (requesting Exec approval):
- Approve 90-day latency SLO carveout for pilot (99.5% @ p95).
- Approve service credit cap of 12.5% for the pilot period only.
- Require a 2-week instrumentation & synthetic validation window prior to pilot start.
- Offer a one-time 15% on-boarding discount on the first month's hosting charges in lieu of broader commercial relief.

Attachments: Draft SLO appendix (Skyline_SLO_Carveout_Draft.pdf) and updated proposal workbook (redwood_proposal_v3.xlsx).

Ben — please confirm any finance flags. If no objections, I will escalate to Jonas for executive clearance.

Marissa Cole
Head of Deal Desk, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
(attachments: Skyline_SLO_Carveout_Draft.pdf; redwood_proposal_v3.xlsx)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: latency SLO carveout & service credit language (Skyline pilot)

Marissa / Avery — I reviewed the ask and Marissa's recommendation. Executive decision: APPROVED with conditions.

Approved items:
- 90-day latency SLO carveout (99.5% p95) for the Skyline pilot.
- Service credit cap set at 12.5% of monthly invoice for the pilot period.
- One-time 15% onboarding discount as commercial offset.

Conditions / guardrails:
1) Instrumentation & synthetic validation must be completed and confirmed by Redwood SRE before pilot goes live.
2) Escrowed metrics export: Skyline must agree to weekly synthetic test reports and grant Redwood limited log access for the pilot window (read-only).
3) This approval is pilot-specific and non-precedential; any future customer requests will be assessed independently.

Marissa, please update the SLO appendix and loop in Legal for an expedited sign-off. Avery — communicate the decisions and conditions to the Skyline contracts contact. Elena — we'll send a final redline and a DocuSign envelope by EOD.

Jonas Weber
VP, Commercial Sales
Redwood Inference
(See attached: approval_note_internal.docx — internal only)
